entities.summary: Vedem was a Czech-language literary magazine that existed from 1942 to 1944 in the Theresienstadt Ghetto in the ghetto of Terezín during the Holocaust. It was hand-produced by a group of teenaged boys, among them editor-in-chief Petr Ginz and Hanuš Hachenburg. Altogether, about 800 pages of Vedem survived World War II.
